scope: One dedicated backend per dispatch; two SDKs sequentially; one strong-random owned queue each; no schema reset or global deletion.
status: Prepared locally only. Root must pin final source identities and publish/dispatch.
placement: Copy standalone module to test/reopen-budget in support branch; install workflow.yml.template separately only when root authorizes publication.
ownership: Fresh exclusive artifact directory and persisted ownership.json precede every Open. Registered queue names are the only cleanup scope. Preflight refuses existing names. Unjoined owner/receiver/provider or absent cleanup proof blocks the next SDK.
lease_contract: QueueConfig uses default 30s, verified via ListQueues, MaxDeliveryCount=1. Actual original lease remaining is recorded at stop. Stop-to-confirmed settlement must fit it. No product transport/retry/lease setting is widened.
protocol_evidence: Exact queue/seq/body/message ID/count/token. Explicit Renew and managed Complete additionally require matching request, HTTP200, explicit ok:true, real EOF and successful Close. Stats empty and handler count one.
measurement: Transport-entry counts, not SQL commit proof. Full window ends after confirmed settlement and Stats. Pending requests at that instant are reported active; provider_joined requires teardown completion. Warm reopen requires zero CREATE and captured version write. Unknown route or incomplete capture invalidates evidence. Background maintenance enabled.
cleanup: Stop/join Receiver and Serve; force-delete only the owned name; inspect full inventory for absence; close all Engine owners and require 200ms provider quiet. Persist failure/owned identity for follow-up.
privacy: No DSN/host/token/header/raw SQL/payload/raw error. Fixed safe fields only. Max64 storage events plus drop count; no cause/error attrs. Fingerprints are correlation aids, not exact causal attribution.
limits: One finite window is not soak/throughput proof.
Unrecognized base_url routes cause inconclusive diagnostic failure.
Killed process may leave owned queue; ownership.json is written before creation for exact recovery.
No remote tests are started by this preparation task.
supplemental_cleanup: After confirming the original process/job has ended, run the same pinned binary with -mode cleanup -owner-exit-confirmed -backend ALIAS -out ORIGINAL_DIRECTORY. It checks backend/source identity, valid registered names and (on the same host) that the original PID is absent. It writes cleanup-result.json separately and never changes the original result.json. Workflow foreground timeout/wait ends before this always-step; an outer runner loss still requires operator confirmation and the same entrypoint. Manual cleanup must run while holding the same turso-verification-db owner lock or after verifying no competing verification job is active.
